summary: M1-S01 re-tested after rebuild #2 (finding F-11). All 6 runnable acceptance tests passed: both always-on structural checks (xml 11/11 parse; manifest 10 files <-> 10 members, two-way consistent, no wildcards) and all 4 declared checkers at exit 0, each paired with check-outputs ok (12/12 declared outputs present, non-empty, parsing). 2 manual tests deferred to the M1 gate, neither ticked here. Step set to tested. Observation only, outside acceptance_tests[]: check_case_management_setup.py exits 0, and its new CMS-STEM-01/02 rules are demonstrably live rather than fail-open -- the same checker over the pre-rebuild artefacts still committed under examples/ emits 4 ERROR lines.
confidence_rationale: Step 7 rubric, HIGH row: every declared test either ran or was correctly classified as manual, both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code observed in this run. No MEDIUM trigger fired -- no command test was refused, no coverage-gap exclusion was needed for any of the six metadata types present, and check-outputs reported no missing, empty or malformed declared output. No LOW trigger fired -- every declared checker resolved to exactly one existing script, the artefact directory holds 13 files, and every exit code was captured to tests/M1-S01/.

process_observations.observation: The CMS-STEM-01/02 green is earned, not fail-open. Rather than trust an exit 0 from rules added the same day, the pre-rebuild copy of these artefacts still committed at examples/builds/case-onboarding/artefacts/M1-S01 was used as a read-only negative control: the same checker emits 4 ERROR lines there (CMS-STEM-01 x2 on the spaced <fullName>, CMS-STEM-02 x2 on the record types referencing them) and is silent on the rebuilt tree. The rule fires on the defect and passes the fix.

Rebuild #2 was surgical and is self-documenting. deploy-order.md carries a Rebuild history section naming F-11 as the cause, a six-row table of exactly what changed, and an explicit statement that the other seven artefacts are byte-identical to rebuild #1. The manifest check confirms the blast radius: only the two BusinessProcess members differ from the run-1 manifest, and both directions of the file/member comparison close at 10.

The manifest's CompactLayout member form has never been exercised by anything that reads package.xml. This step declares the bare member Case_Intake, which is what skills/admin/list-views-and-compact-layouts/references/metadata-examples.md specifies ('compact layout name'), and that is the form the manifest check was judged against. But the mock deploy that validated 12/12 ran sf project deploy start --source-dir --dry-run, so the CLI derived members from the source tree itself and never read this package.xml -- and reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md records the component it derived as the object-qualified CompactLayout Case.Case_Intake. The two forms disagree, and deploy-order.md independently flags this member as 'the thinnest grounding in this manifest'. Nothing in the build has yet deployed via --manifest, so a member-form defect here would still be invisible.

Manual test 1's counter-example is stale after rebuild #2. It reads 'the BARE process name (not Case.Support Process)', a form that predates the fix and is now wrong on two counts at once -- object-qualified and spaced. The assertion it guards still holds against the artefacts on disk, so this is not a failure, but a human ticking it at the gate is comparing against an illustration the rebuild invalidated. The plan owns the text; this agent does not edit acceptance-test descriptions.

The step's inputs and its artefacts still disagree about the business-process names, which is F-11's unclosed planner half. plan.json.steps[M1-S01].inputs.business_processes reads ['Support Process', 'Billing Process'] -- the spaced form -- while outputs[], the files and the manifest are all stem form. Nothing downstream reads that input string today, so no test can fail on it, and neither this agent nor build-step-runner may edit a plan field beyond its own status transition. It closes at plan v6 or not at all.

Two declared checkers on this step carry no scope field and so default to step scope, and one of them is on the documented cross-referential list. check_list_views_and_compact_layouts.py is declared at scope step with a written justification that step scope is the only scope at which it can pass here, because rule 6 needs the compactLayoutAssignment and the field-type lookup inside this step's own tree -- an argued exception rather than an oversight. Worth recording that the argument, not the default, is what makes it correct.

build_plan.py emitted three WARNs on unrelated steps while writing this status transition -- M5-S02 acceptance_tests[0], M5-S04 acceptance_tests[0] and [3] each declare a checker with a non-standard argument form that step-tester will run verbatim. They did not affect this step and are the known unconverged-checker-flag follow-up in standards/build-orchestration.md section 5, but they will land on whoever tests M5.
M1-S01 is tested and its documentation predates rebuild #2, so the doc keeper is the next stage of the loop.
